name: Phalura
notes: Phalura/Palula (Dardic, Indo-Aryan; Chitral, Pakistan) in Palula common transcription (PCT), the indological-style Latin transcription used by Liljegren and other Shina-variety scholars (Liljegren 2016, ch. 1.8) -- not the community's Arabic-based practical orthography, which this spec does not cover. Retroflex ṭ/ḍ/ṇ/ṣ/ṛ/c̣, the caron series č/š/ǰ (alveolo-palatal ʨ/ɕ/ʑ), and marginal ẓ/q/f/x/ɣ follow the PCT-to-IPA correspondence in Liljegren (2016), Table 1.8 and the consonant inventory in Table 3.1/2.1. ǰ is mapped to its phonemic value /ʑ/ per Table 1.8, even though the same source's phonology chapter (Table 3.1 discussion) notes the affricate [dʑ] is the more common surface allophone (especially in the A dialect) and the gold's transcriptions reflect that surface form; the phonemic PCT correspondence is kept. Aspirate digraphs and acute tone/accent marks are Latin practical additions; doubled vowels rendered long. Stress exemption: Phalura (Palula) has a lexical pitch-accent system that is only partially predictable and not consistently marked in the orthography modeled here; no stress block is declared. Sources: Liljegren, Henrik (2008), Towards a grammatical description of Palula, ch. on prosody; Liljegren, Henrik (2016), A Grammar of Palula, Language Science Press (open access), ch. 1.7-1.8 (orthography/PCT), ch. 2.1 and 3.1 (phoneme inventory).
